questions.stem: A patient with asthma is tachypneic and has an early respiratory alkalosis. Later, the patient's breathing becomes ineffective and carbon dioxide rises. What best explains the later change?

options.text: Airflow obstruction limits carbon dioxide elimination
Renal loss of bicarbonate causes metabolic alkalosis
Fibrin dissolves in the pulmonary circulation
Erythropoietin secretion increases

questions.rationale: Worsening obstruction can impair ventilation and lead to carbon dioxide retention and respiratory acidosis.
questions.draftNote: Unreviewed addition; requires source and semantic duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with a large pulmonary embolism develops signs of right ventricular strain. Which change most directly increases the ventricle's workload?

options.text: Increased resistance in pulmonary circulation
Reduced systemic blood viscosity
Increased filtration through the kidneys
Decreased pressure in pulmonary arteries

questions.rationale: Obstruction and hypoxic vasoconstriction raise pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular workload.
questions.draftNote: Unreviewed addition; requires source and semantic duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with a prior gastric bypass reports fatigue and tingling in the feet. Which anemia should the nurse consider?

options.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia
Iron deficiency anemia as the only possible explanation
Polycythemia
Thrombocytosis

questions.rationale: The worksheet links gastric bypass to impaired B12 absorption and identifies paresthesias with B12 deficiency.

questions.stem: A patient with dysuria and urgency subsequently develops fever and costovertebral angle tenderness. What does the change suggest?

options.text: Infection may have ascended to the kidneys
The infection is now limited to the urethral opening
A pulmonary artery is obstructed
A factor VIII deficiency has developed

questions.rationale: Fever and costovertebral angle tenderness support possible upper urinary tract involvement.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced CKD develops hyperkalemia and peaked T waves after missed dialysis. Which problem should the nurse recognize?

options.text: Reduced potassium removal with a risk of cardiac effects
Excess potassium excretion is causing hypokalemia
The kidneys are producing excess erythropoietin
Vitamin B12 is directly occluding the ureters

questions.rationale: Advanced kidney dysfunction reduces potassium excretion; the quiz links missed dialysis and peaked T waves with hyperkalemia.

questions.stem: A ventilated patient has pooled oral secretions. Which nursing activity addresses a factor associated with ventilator-associated pneumonia in the worksheet?

options.text: Providing oral care and managing secretions
Limiting all oral care
Keeping secretions pooled in the mouth
Avoiding assessment of the airway

questions.rationale: The worksheet links ventilator-associated pneumonia risk to inadequate oral care and pooled secretions.

questions.stem: An older patient with pneumonia has a productive cough and fever. Which auscultation finding over the infected area is consistent with the worksheet?

options.text: Crackles or coarse rales
An absent bowel sound
A vascular bruit over the kidney
A heart murmur only

questions.rationale: Productive cough and crackles or coarse rales over the affected site are listed pneumonia findings.

questions.stem: A patient with a positive TB test has no fever, cough, night sweats, or weight loss and is diagnosed with latent infection. What is the most appropriate interpretation?

options.text: The infection is inactive and is not spread to others
Active pulmonary TB is established by the test alone
The patient must have miliary TB
The absence of symptoms excludes previous exposure

questions.rationale: Latent TB may produce a positive test without symptoms and is not contagious.

questions.stem: A patient rapidly breathes during an early asthma attack. Which acid-base disturbance may initially occur from increased ventilation?

options.text: Respiratory alkalosis
Metabolic acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis due to bicarbonate gain
Respiratory acidosis due to immediate carbon dioxide retention in every case

questions.rationale: The worksheet describes early tachypnea causing respiratory alkalosis; severe ventilation failure may later cause respiratory acidosis.
questions.draftNote: Candidate requires independent source and duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with stable COPD has chronic carbon dioxide retention and elevated bicarbonate. Which interpretation is most consistent with renal compensation?

options.text: The kidneys retain bicarbonate to help compensate for chronic respiratory acidosis
The elevated bicarbonate proves all lung disease has resolved
The low oxygen level means gas exchange is unaffected
Compensation requires an immediate return of carbon dioxide to normal

questions.rationale: In chronic carbon dioxide retention, renal bicarbonate retention can help compensate for respiratory acidosis.

questions.stem: A patient with heart failure develops a pleural effusion related to increased hydrostatic pressure. Which type of fluid is most consistent with that mechanism?

options.text: Transudate
Empyema from pleural infection
Blood from penetrating trauma
Air from a pneumothorax

questions.rationale: The worksheet associates transudative effusions with altered hydrostatic or oncotic pressure, including in heart failure.
questions.draftNote: Candidate requires independent source and duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient has recurrent spontaneous joint bleeding. A second patient has petechiae and gum bleeding. Which comparison best fits the worksheet?

options.text: The first pattern suggests a coagulation factor problem; the second suggests a platelet problem
Both patterns uniquely identify platelet excess
Both patterns prove a urinary tract infection
Joint bleeding is the defining finding of a normal coagulation system

questions.rationale: Deep joint bleeding is associated with coagulation factor problems; petechiae and gum bleeding fit platelet-related bleeding.

questions.stem: A patient reports heavy menstrual bleeding and fatigue. Why does chronic blood loss increase the risk of iron deficiency anemia?

options.text: Iron contained in lost blood is not available for normal recycling
Blood loss directly increases the body's iron stores
Chronic bleeding always increases intrinsic factor production
The body converts lost blood into additional platelets

questions.rationale: The worksheet explains that iron lost with blood cannot be recycled, increasing iron deficiency risk.

questions.stem: A patient with vitamin B12 deficiency asks why intrinsic factor matters. Which explanation is consistent with the worksheet?

options.text: Intrinsic factor supports vitamin B12 absorption in the ileum
Intrinsic factor converts iron directly into platelets
Intrinsic factor produces fibrin in the pleural space
Intrinsic factor prevents all urinary stones

questions.rationale: Intrinsic factor is released by gastric mucosa and is needed for B12 absorption in the ileum.

questions.stem: A patient with sickle cell anemia develops severe pain during an infection. Which process is most directly responsible for a vaso-occlusive pain crisis?

options.text: Sickled cells obstruct blood flow, causing tissue hypoxia
All red cells rapidly become larger and transport more oxygen
The lungs produce intrinsic factor
Platelets dissolve ureteral stones

questions.rationale: Sickling can obstruct vessels and impair blood flow, causing tissue hypoxia and pain.

Chronic leukemia always resolves in hours without treatment
Acute leukemia involves only platelets and never white cells
Neither form affects blood cell production

Avoid emptying the bladder

Prerenal from dehydration alone

options.text: Reduced acid excretion and impaired bicarbonate generation
Excessive carbon dioxide removal by the lungs
Excessive removal of every hydrogen ion
Increased fibrin production in urine

questions.rationale: The worksheet explains that kidneys with advanced dysfunction cannot adequately excrete acid or generate bicarbonate.

questions.stem: A patient undergoing peritoneal dialysis has fluid placed in the abdomen. What permits exchange of wastes and water with the dialysate?

options.text: The peritoneal membrane acts as a semipermeable barrier
The pleural cavity functions as the dialysis cartridge
The patient's red cells become the dialysate
The ureter replaces the peritoneal membrane

questions.rationale: Peritoneal dialysis uses the peritoneal membrane for diffusion and osmosis between blood and dialysate.
